project.objective: Besides their children John, Hannah Grace, Edwin, William, and James, did Hannah Earnest and Edwin Grice have any other children? Identify each additional child and their birth details.

questions.question: Who were all the children born to Hannah Earnest and Edwin Grice, of West Bromwich and Birmingham, Staffordshire/Warwickshire, England, beyond the five already recorded in the tree (John, Hannah Grace, Edwin, William, and James)?
questions.rationale: The objective is to enumerate any children of this couple beyond the five known in the tree. English civil registration (from 1837), decennial census records (1881, 1891, 1901, 1911), and parish registers covering West Bromwich and Birmingham are well-preserved and digitised, giving strong prospects for a complete tally. Searching these records against the known children's birth span (1877–1886) and beyond will reveal any gaps or additional children.

items.rationale: The 1911 England census is the definitive source for this enumerative question: it records for each married woman the total children born alive, the number still living, and the number who died. Hannah Earnest (born 1857) would be approximately 54 in 1911; locating her household immediately establishes the total count and shows how many additional children to seek in earlier records. loc_001 identifies this as the most important single record for the question. All five known children's 1891 residence facts place the household in Birmingham (confirmed from the tree for John, Edwin Jr., William and James), and James Grice's 1911 residence is also Birmingham, making Birmingham the primary search jurisdiction.

items.jurisdiction: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
items.rationale: The tree records the 1881 household in West Bromwich (John b.1877 and Hannah Grace b.1880, christened there 5 May 1880, both show 1881 West Bromwich residence). Edwin Grice was born 1854 in West Bromwich and was resident there in 1881. The 1881 census is therefore the household listing during the couple's main childbearing period to that point, and may surface a child between John (1877) and Hannah Grace (1880) or one born before 1881 not yet in the tree. The 1861 and 1871 censuses show the parents before the first known child and confirm whether any earlier children appear. Edwin Jr. born 1883 in Darlaston suggests the family may have lived briefly in Darlaston; also check the Darlaston area enumeration in the 1881 returns.

By 1891 the household had moved to Birmingham (confirmed by residence facts for John, Edwin Jr., William and James). The 1891 census shows all children still living at home at that date; the 1901 census shows any remaining younger children not yet independent. Cross-referencing the 1891 and 1901 household listings against item 2 reveals children who died between 1881 and 1891, and surfaces any additional younger children born after the 1881 census who are not yet in the tree. Hannah born 1857 would be 34 in 1891 and 44 in 1901, so further births in the 1887-1897 window are plausible.

items.jurisdiction: West Bromwich Registration District and Birmingham Registration District, England
items.repository: FreeBMD / West Midlands BMD / Staffordshire BMD
items.rationale: Civil registration became effectively complete after 1875 when non-compliance penalties were introduced (loc_001). Search the surname 'Grice' (and variants: Grise, Gryce) in West Bromwich Registration District and Birmingham Registration District, all quarters 1875-1902 (Hannah born 1857, approximately 45 by 1902). Also search the Darlaston RD given Edwin Jr.'s 1883 birth there. loc_001 instructs use of all three free indexes—FreeBMD (freebmd.org.uk), West Midlands BMD (westmidlandsbmd.org.uk) and Staffordshire BMD (staffordshirebmd.org.uk)—as they differ in coverage. Before Q1 1911, the index records only child surname, quarter and registration district; for any candidate not matched to a known child, order a GRO birth certificate to verify the mother's maiden name 'Earnest.'

items.jurisdiction: West Bromwich Registration District and Birmingham Registration District, England
items.rationale: Children who died in infancy or early childhood leave no census trace but appear in the GRO death index. Search FreeBMD and West Midlands BMD for 'Grice' deaths (and variants) in West Bromwich RD and Birmingham RD, 1875-1920, filtering for ages 0-15. Any death entry not attributable to a known child is a candidate additional child; order a GRO death certificate to confirm the parents' names and address. loc_001 flags the significance of name reuse: in English families of this period, reuse of a given name almost always signals that the first child of that name died before the next was given it—a 'second John' or 'second Hannah' in the death index is evidence of a previously unknown child of the same name.

items.jurisdiction: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
items.rationale: loc_001 notes that the FamilySearch Catalog holds 45 hits for West Bromwich including parish records, and that Anglican parish registers cover only a portion of baptisms given the strong Nonconformist presence. The catalog entries are browse-only (personCount 0). Browse each West Bromwich Anglican parish register for 'Grice' baptisms 1875-1902. Hannah Grace's christening on 5 May 1880 at West Bromwich (recorded in the tree) anchors the search: the same registers that recorded her may hold additional Grice baptisms not surfaced by the GRO index. After the family moved to Birmingham by 1891, also check Birmingham Anglican parish registers in the catalog for Grice baptisms 1891-1902.

items.jurisdiction: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
items.rationale: loc_001 identifies an exceptionally strong Nonconformist presence in West Bromwich: five Wesleyan chapels, four Independent chapels and two Baptist chapels. A family affiliated with any of these would have children baptized in nonconformist registers rather than Anglican ones, and would not appear in the item 6 parish search. Search Ancestry's England nonconformist baptism collections for 'Grice' in West Bromwich chapel registers, 1875-1902. FamilySearch may also hold some nonconformist registers via the catalog; check there as well. The Catholic church (St. Michael and Holy Angels, registrations from 1832 per loc_001) is a lower probability but can be checked if Wesleyan and Independent sources are exhausted.

Edwin Grice (born 1854, West Bromwich) may have left a will or intestacy record naming his surviving children as beneficiaries or next of kin. A will frequently lists all surviving children; a grant of administration names the next of kin. Either establishes a roster of surviving children at Edwin's death and may reveal a child not surfaced by census or civil registration. The date range 1890-1935 is bounded by Edwin's plausible lifespan: earliest plausible death at approximately age 36 in 1890, upper bound approximately age 81 in 1935. If Edwin's probate is not found, also search for Hannah's probate, which would likewise name her surviving children.

items.jurisdiction: West Bromwich Registration District and Birmingham Registration District, England
items.rationale: Marriage records for the children serve two purposes. First, any 'Grice' marriage in West Bromwich RD or Birmingham RD not attributable to a known child is a candidate additional child; GRO marriage certificates name both fathers, confirming whether 'Edwin Grice' is stated. Second, marriage witnesses are frequently siblings: a known child's marriage certificate may name an otherwise unrecorded sibling as witness, directly revealing an additional child of the couple. The date range 1894-1930 covers the earliest plausible marriage for John (born 1877, minimum age 17 in 1894) through the latest plausible marriage for James (born 1886). Search FreeBMD and West Midlands BMD for 'Grice' marriages in both districts.

log.notes: 1891 census search for Hannah Grice with spouse Edwin Grice, Birmingham, Warwickshire. Top match (rank 1) is 'Household of Edwin Grice', Birmingham 1891, Hannah Grice female, birth 1855 (2-year gap from expected 1857, within census tolerance), Staffordshire, married, Edwin Grice as spouse confirmed present. Already attached to subject. All other 7 results have large birth-year conflicts and are clearly not the subject.

1901 census search for Hannah Grice with spouse Edwin Grice, Birmingham, Warwickshire. 7 results returned but none score above 0.01; all have large birth-year conflicts. Real negative for this query shape — will retry with Edwin as principal.

1901 census search with Edwin Grice as principal, Hannah as spouse, Birmingham, Warwickshire. 13 results, none scored above 0.01; all have large birth-year conflicts. Real negative for this query shape. Will try broader search without place restriction.

1901 census broader England-wide search for Edwin Grice with Hannah as spouse, no place restriction. 295 total; 50 returned. Rank 21 (searchRank 1) is Edwin Grice married to Hannah Grice in Quarry Bank, Staffordshire — different couple (Edwin b.1848 Quarry Bank, birthYearGap -9). No candidate scored above 0.01. Real negative for this query shape. Will try Hannah as principal, England-wide, no spouse filter.

1901 census England-wide search for Hannah Grice female b.1852-1862, no place or spouse filter. 14 results; no candidate scored above 0.01. Top match (rank 1) Hannah Grice, married, Rowley Regis, Staffordshire, b.1857, 'Household of John Grice' — exact birth year but birthplace indexed as Cradley Heath (conflicts with known Darlaston). Match score 0.0045, attached to other. Needs further investigation. Rank 3 is the Quarry Bank Hannah Grice (b.1852) in a different Edwin Grice household — clearly not subject. After 5 search attempts across different query shapes, no confident 1901 match found. The 1901 record may be unindexed or Edwin may have died before 1901.

Read 1901 census 'Household of John Grice', Rowley Regis, Staffordshire — the top-scoring 1901 candidate for Hannah Grice. Confirmed as a different family: head is John Grice b.1858 Quarry Bank (not Edwin), Hannah is his wife b.1857 Cradley Heath (not Darlaston), children all born Cradley Heath. Not the subject's household. Recorded as namesake.

1881 England census (collection 2562194), Edwin Grice b.1854 West Bromwich, residence West Bromwich. 3 results; searchRank-1 hit is 'Household of Edwin Grice', West Bromwich, married factory laborer b.1854 West Bromwich — contextually the target household. Low matchScore because Hannah is the subject but Edwin is the principal. Attached to other (Edwin's own tree entry). Full household read in a separate record_read entry.
1871 census collection-pinned (1538354), Hannah Earnest b.1857, Staffordshire. Zero results. Retried without collection pin.

1871 unpinned retry: 270 results. Top 2 matches are marriage records (collection 2364451, Staffordshire Church Records) for Hannah Ernest marrying Edwin Grice, 26 Mar 1876, West Bromwich, matchScore 0.562 — not a 1871 census record. No 1871 census record for Hannah Earnest identified in any of the top 50 results. The marriage record (QLQH-5V5Z / QLQH-5VGT) is a significant collateral find for this family.

1861 England census (collection 1493747), Hannah Earnest b.1857 in Staffordshire. Top hit: Hannah Earnest b.1858 Darlaston, Household of Joseph Earnest, Blakemores Lane, Darlaston — matchScore 0.689, already attached to subject. Second result is a Wales male — discard.

Read 1861 Household of Joseph Earnest (ark M7ZT-RWG). England 1861 census records relationship to head. Confirmed household: Joseph Earnest (head, b.1827 Potteries, iron labourer, married), Diana Earnest (wife, b.1837 Darlaston), Elizabeth (b.1851 Darlaston), Fanny (b.1853 Darlaston), Hannah (b.1858 Darlaston — our subject), John (b.1861 Darlaston). Joseph and Diana Earnest confirmed as Hannah's parents. No child between Fanny (1853) and Hannah (1858) in 1861.

Read 1881 Household of Edwin Grice, West Bromwich (ark Q27F-Z3WX). England 1881 census records relationship to head explicitly. Household: Edwin Grice (head, b.1854 W.Bromwich, factory laborer, married), Hannah Grice (wife, b.1857 Darlaston), John Grice (b.1877 W.Bromwich, single), Lydia Grice (b.1879 W.Bromwich, single), Hannah Grace Grice (b.1880 W.Bromwich, single). No additional children found — 3 children enumerated in April 1881.

1881 census (collection 2562194), Edwin Grice b.1854 in Darlaston, Staffordshire. 3 results returned but all are from non-Darlaston Staffordshire locations (West Bromwich, Enville, Tutbury). The Edwin Grice West Bromwich household appears again (same as first search). No Edwin Grice household in Darlaston in 1881. Confirms the family was in West Bromwich, not Darlaston, at the time of the April 1881 census.
1871 census collection-pinned (1538354), Joseph Earnest b.1827, Staffordshire. Zero results. Also tried 'Ernest' spelling with collection pin — also nil. Retried without collection pin in next entry.

1871 unpinned retry for Joseph Earnest b.1827, Staffordshire: 256 results, top matches are marriage and Staffordshire church records (collection 2364451) — no 1871 census result. Notable collateral finds: marriage of Joseph Earnest to Dinah Hines, 23 Dec 1849, Wednesbury (QLQH-JDKQ/QLQH-JDJP); death registration Joseph Ernest b.1827 d.1895 West Bromwich (2JGR-VRC); Joseph Ernest listed on Elizabeth Ernest church record (QL3T-C6BP) and on Hannah Ernest church record (QL3T-C615) in collection 2364451 — possible christening records for Hannah and her sibling. Both surname spellings exhausted for 1871 census. Household not indexed in 1871 FamilySearch census under any surname variant tried.

quirks: Civil registration began 1 July 1837 by national legislation; administered through Registration Districts (West Bromwich RD; Birmingham RD). Coverage was not universal before 1875 when penalties were introduced for non-compliance.
West Bromwich was in the West Bromwich Registration District; Birmingham was in the Birmingham Registration District; searching by district name in GRO indexes is essential.
Both West Bromwich (Staffordshire) and Birmingham (Warwickshire) transferred to the new county of West Midlands in 1974; records created before 1974 are filed under the original county names.

West Bromwich had an exceptionally strong Nonconformist presence: five Wesleyan chapels, four Independent chapels, two Baptist chapels, and a Roman Catholic church. Anglican parish registers cover only a portion of baptisms; search nonconformist registers systematically.
Catholic records for St. Michael and Holy Angels, West Bromwich begin in 1832, but earlier entries are held at Walsall; check Walsall for any Catholic events before the West Bromwich registers open.
The 1911 census is the most direct source for total children born to a couple: it records total children born alive, number still living, and number who died.
GRO indexes are quarterly; a birth registered after the quarter of birth appears in the following quarter.
In English families, reuse of a child's given name almost always meant the first child of that name died before the second was given the same name.

West Midlands BMD (http://www.westmidlandsbmd.org.uk/) and Staffordshire BMD (http://www.staffordshirebmd.org.uk/) provide free regional indexes that differ from the national FreeBMD index; use all three.

Volume search for West Bromwich as a Town returned 0 FamilySearch-digitized volumes for 1860-1920; records appear instead in the FamilySearch Catalog (45 hits) including census returns and parish records.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: West Bromwich (Staffordshire) and Birmingham (Warwickshire), England (1860–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **West Bromwich:** Ancient settlement; civil registration district from 1 July 1837. Part of Staffordshire until 1974 when it transferred to the new county of West Midlands.
- **Birmingham:** Ancient borough in Warwickshire; civil registration district from 1 July 1837. Transferred to West Midlands in 1974.
- **County seat / administrative center:** Stafford (Staffordshire); Warwick (Warwickshire)
- **Economy:** Heavy industry (iron, steel, metalworking, manufactured goods). West Bromwich was part of the Black Country; Birmingham was the principal manufacturing city of the Midlands.
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly English; significant Welsh and Irish migration into industrial areas.
- **Religious denominations:** Church of England; Wesleyan Methodists (five chapels in West Bromwich alone); Independents (four chapels); Baptists (two chapels); Primitive Methodists; Roman Catholics (St. Michael and Holy Angels, West Bromwich from 1832); many denominations in Birmingham.
- **Key historical events:** Rapid industrial urbanization; WWI (1914–1918).

## Boundary changes
- Both places were stable within their historic counties throughout 1860–1920.
- In 1974, both transferred from their historic counties to the new metropolitan county of West Midlands. Records created before 1974 are filed under the original county names.
- The West Bromwich civil registration district was coterminous with the town throughout this period.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** 1 July 1837, national legislation administered through Registration Districts (West Bromwich Registration District; Birmingham Registration District). Source: [England Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration)
- **What exists:** Births, marriages, and deaths from 1837 to present, registered quarterly. Coverage not universal before 1875; near-complete since 1875.
- **Where held:** Original registers at local register offices. National GRO quarterly index searchable at:
  - FamilySearch: [England and Wales Birth Registration Index, 1837–2008](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2285338) (free, indexed)
  - FamilySearch: [England and Wales Marriage Registration Index, 1837–2005](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2285732) (free, indexed)
  - FamilySearch: [England and Wales Death Registration Index, 1837–2007](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2285341) (free, indexed)
  - FreeBMD (http://freebmd.org.uk/): free national volunteer index, 1837–1983
  - West Midlands BMD (http://www.westmidlandsbmd.org.uk/): free regional index for West Bromwich and Birmingham
  - Staffordshire BMD (http://www.staffordshirebmd.org.uk/): free county index (not yet complete for all years)
  - Ancestry: [Staffordshire, England, Birth, Marriage and Death Indexes, 1837–2017](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61709/) (subscription, indexed)
- **Gaps:** Some pre-1875 births were not registered. Events indexed by quarter registered, not date of occurrence.
- **Certificates:** Order from GRO (https://www.gro.gov.uk/) or local register office.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of England (All Saints as the ancient parish from 1608, with daughter parishes Christ Church from 1829, Holy Trinity from 1841, St. Paul, St. Peter, and others); Wesleyan Methodist; Independent/Congregational; Baptist; Primitive Methodist; Roman Catholic (St. Michael and Holy Angels from 1832); many more in Birmingham.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations. Nonconformist registers often include births and deaths.
- **Where held:**
  - Church of England: Staffordshire Record Office (West Bromwich parishes); Library of Birmingham/Archives (Birmingham parishes)
  - Nonconformist pre-1837: The National Archives (most deposited centrally); also FamilySearch catalog koha:95994, koha:96001, koha:95998 for West Bromwich chapel registers (Mare's Green Chapel, The Old Meeting, Wesleyan Church)
  - Catholic: Birmingham Archdiocesan Archives (http://www.birminghamarchdiocesanarchives.org.uk/); FamilySearch has microfilmed St. Michael and Holy Angels records 1832–1995 (catalog entries koha:762327)
  - FamilySearch: [England, Staffordshire, Church Records, 1538–1944](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2364451) — indexed + images (free)
  - Ancestry: [Birmingham, England, Church of England Baptisms, 1813–1919](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/4981) — indexed (subscription)
  - Ancestry: [Staffordshire, England, Church of England Births and Baptisms, 1813–1900](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62292/) — indexed (subscription)
  - FamilySearch catalog: Bishop's transcripts of All Saints Church (West Bromwich), 1676–1868 (catalog entry koha:327194; available at FamilySearch Centers)
- **Gaps:** No surviving parish registers listed for West Bromwich St. James (formerly Hill Top) in the FamilySearch Wiki. Some nonconformist registers were not deposited centrally.
- **Language:** English throughout.
- **Important note — Catholic records:** For St. Michael and Holy Angels, catalog notes 'Earlier entries can be found at Walsall.' Search Walsall for Catholic baptisms before the West Bromwich registers begin (1832).
- **Parish affiliation note:** The affiliation of specific nonconformist congregations in West Bromwich with particular church registers has not been fully confirmed in this survey; consult GENUKI (http://www.genuki.org.uk/big/eng/STS/WestBromwich/) and the Staffordshire Record Office to identify which register covers a given congregation.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** 1861–1921, all indexed with images at FamilySearch and major subscription sites.
  - FamilySearch catalog entry koha:583890 confirms West Bromwich census returns 1841–1891 specifically online.
  - 1921 census at Ancestry and Findmypast (subscription).
  - **The 1911 census is essential for this research question:** records total children born alive, number still living, number who died per married woman. Source: [England Census](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Census)
- **State/provincial census:** None in England.
- **1939 Register:** Available at Ancestry and Findmypast (subscription); useful for older children's whereabouts.
- **Missing:** 1931 census destroyed in a 1942 fire. No 1941 census taken.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills (testate), letters of administration (intestate), inventories, guardianship records.
- **Date range:** From 1837; before 1858 under the Court of the Bishop of Lichfield (Episcopal Consistory).
- **Where held:** Pre-1858: Lichfield Joint Record Office. Post-1858: Principal Registry of the Family Division; indexed in [England & Wales National Probate Calendar, 1858–1995](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1904) on Ancestry (subscription).

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds.
- **Types:** Deeds, land tax assessments. Catalog koha:410643 covers land tax assessments for West Bromwich, 1772–1831.
- **Where held:** Staffordshire Record Office (West Bromwich); Library of Birmingham/Archives (Birmingham).
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Crown grants via local conveyances; deeds at Staffordshire Record Office.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** WWI (1914–1918); Boer War (1899–1902).
- **Record types:** Service records, pension records, medal rolls, casualty rolls.
- FamilySearch: [UK, World War I Service Records, 1914–1920](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2125045) — indexed + images (free)
- **Where held:** The National Archives, Kew; many online at FamilySearch, Ancestry, Findmypast.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Heath Lane Cemetery, West Bromwich (burial registers 1859–1905 transcribed by FreeReg); Mayers Green Congregational Church graveyard (tombstone record at catalog koha:628392); Christ Church graveyard monumental inscriptions (catalog koha:482815); Birmingham city cemeteries — Witton, Yardley, Handsworth, Key Hill.
- **Online coverage:** Ancestry: [Birmingham, England Cemetery and Crematoria Records, 1836–2017](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/70926) (subscription); Deceased Online (http://www.deceasedonline.com/); FindAGrave.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Birmingham Daily Gazette (1862–1956), Birmingham Daily Post (1857–1999), Birmingham Mail (1871–1999), Aris's Birmingham Gazette (1741–1880), Birmingham Suburban Times (1884–1901) — all at Findmypast (subscription); British Newspaper Archive (http://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/).
- **Content value:** Obituaries, birth and marriage announcements, inquests.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Record types:** Outgoing passenger lists, naturalization records.
- FamilySearch: [UK, Outgoing Passenger Lists, 1890–1960](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/4229516) — indexed + images (free).
- **Content note:** Passenger lists record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. Examine the full manifest for all family members.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Land tax assessments, rate books.
- **Date range:** Land tax assessments for West Bromwich 1772–1831 in catalog (koha:410643). Rate books from later periods at Staffordshire Record Office.
- **Substitute value:** Rate books can help fill gaps between census years.

### Other record types
- **School records:** FamilySearch catalog entries for West Bromwich school records 1892–1909 (olib:2744917) and Trinity C.E. School 1909–1914 (olib:2744918), available at FamilySearch Centers.
- **Poor law records:** West Bromwich Poor Law Union (1834–1930); workhouse records at http://www.workhouses.org.uk/WestBromwich/.
- **Genealogical society:** Birmingham and Midland Society for Genealogy and Heraldry (http://www.bmsgh.org/) — the main society for Staffordshire, Warwickshire, and Worcestershire, holding compiled records and indexes.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | England, Staffordshire, Church Records 1538–1944 (coll. 2364451); England & Wales Birth/Marriage/Death Registration Indexes 1837–2008/2005/2007; Census 1841–1911; UK WWI Service Records 1914–1920 | Staffordshire church records (indexed + images); civil registration national index; census; military | Free |
| FreeBMD (http://freebmd.org.uk/) | National civil registration index 1837–1983 | Alternative national BMD index not duplicating GRO indexes | Free |
| West Midlands BMD (http://www.westmidlandsbmd.org.uk/) | Local registration district indexes covering West Bromwich and Birmingham | Local BMD records (not yet complete for all years) | Free |
| Staffordshire BMD (http://www.staffordshirebmd.org.uk/) | Staffordshire Registration Service indexes post-1837 | Staffordshire district BMD records | Free |
| Ancestry | Staffordshire, England, Birth, Marriage and Death Indexes 1837–2017 (coll. 61709); Birmingham, England, Church of England Baptisms 1813–1919 (coll. 4981); England & Wales civil registration indexes; census 1841–1921; Birmingham Cemetery Records 1836–2017 (coll. 70926) | Staffordshire BMD indexes; Birmingham church baptisms; full census range; cemetery records | Subscription |
| Findmypast | Staffordshire Parish Registers Browse 1538–1900; Birmingham newspapers 1741–1999; National Burial Index | Parish registers (browse-only images for Staffordshire); newspaper records | Subscription |
| Birmingham Archdiocesan Archives (http://www.birminghamarchdiocesanarchives.org.uk/) | Catholic parish records including St. Michael and Holy Angels, West Bromwich | Catholic baptisms, marriages, burials not yet fully online | Contact required |

**Coverage of this survey:** Volume search for West Bromwich Town returned 0 FamilySearch-digitized volumes indexed for 1860–1920; records appear instead in the FamilySearch Catalog (45 total hits), including census volumes and parish records. Volume search for Birmingham City returned 403 digitized volumes for the period (10 were detailed here, 393 were not examined); the full summary shows 109 baptism volumes (83 browse-only), 66 marriage volumes (61 browse-only), and 74 vital record volumes (63 browse-only).

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Staffordshire Record Office (Stafford) | West Bromwich parish registers; bishop's transcripts; county records | In-person / online request |
| Library of Birmingham / Archives (Centenary Square, Birmingham B1 2ND; tel. 0121 242 4242) | Birmingham parish registers; local history records | In-person |
| Lichfield Joint Record Office | Diocese of Lichfield records; bishop's transcripts; pre-1858 probate | In-person / research enquiry |
| Birmingham Register Office (Holliday Street, Birmingham B1 1TJ; tel. 0121 675 1000) | Original civil registration registers from 1837 | In-person / written application |
| The National Archives (Kew) | Nonconformist registers pre-1837; military records; central government records | In-person / online (many records digitized) |
| Birmingham Archdiocesan Archives | Catholic parish records for the Archdiocese | Contact required |

## Records NOT online
- Original civil registration certificates (must be ordered from GRO or local register office).
- Many Birmingham parish registers for smaller parishes not yet digitized.
- West Bromwich rate books and vestry minute books.
- School admission registers (some partially available via catalog).
- West Bromwich Poor Law Union records beyond what FreeReg has indexed.

## Known record losses
- The 1931 census was destroyed in a fire in 1942, confirmed by the [England Census wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Census). No census substitute covering 1931 was identified for this area in this survey.
- No tool result identified destruction of any specific West Bromwich or Birmingham BMD or parish record sets.

## Research tips
- **Search the 1911 census first.** It records for every married woman: total children born alive, number still living, and number who died — the most direct answer to whether Hannah and Edwin Grice had additional children. Source: [England Census](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Census)
- **Work through every census in sequence** (1861, 1871, 1881, 1891, 1901, 1911). Children appear, age, and may leave the household — tracking them decade by decade reveals individuals who died young and may not appear in later records. Source: [England Research Tips and Strategies](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Research_Tips_and_Strategies)
- **GRO indexes are quarterly.** A birth registered after the quarter of birth appears in the following quarter. Always check the adjacent quarter if the expected one yields nothing. Source: [England Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration)
- **Nonconformist registers were the norm in West Bromwich.** Because Wesleyan, Independent, Baptist, and other chapels outnumbered Anglican churches, search nonconformist registers systematically for any baptism not found in Church of England records. Source: [West Bromwich All Saints, Staffordshire, England Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/West_Bromwich_All_Saints,_Staffordshire,_England_Genealogy)
- **Reuse of a child's name signals earlier death.** Per English naming customs, the same first name given to two successive children of the same sex almost always means the first died before the second was named. Source: [England Naming Customs](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Naming_Customs)
- **Use all three free BMD indexes.** FreeBMD (national), West Midlands BMD (regional), and Staffordshire BMD (county) are independent volunteer projects; a birth not found in one may appear in another.

namesakes.name: Hannah Grice
namesakes.notes: Wife of John Grice (b.1858 Quarry Bank, Gas Tube Fitting Maker). Different head of household (John, not Edwin), different birthplace (Cradley Heath, not Darlaston), all children born Cradley Heath: Benjamin b.1882, Alice b.1883, Tom b.1885, John Jr. b.1888, Samuel b.1891, Albert b.1893. Ruled out as the research subject.
